title: Munich agreement
summary: On 30 September 1938 Germany, Britain, France and Italy agreed at Munich that Czechoslovakia would cede the Sudetenland, where some three million German speakers lived, and Czechoslovakia — which was not at the table, and which had a French alliance and a Soviet undertaking — was told to accept. Chamberlain came home saying it was peace for our time; the rest of the Czech lands were occupied in March 1939. The word Munich has meant the purchase of peace by the sacrifice of a third party ever since, and the atlas holds it as the moment appeasement was tested to destruction.
